finding: Japanese armor production sources mix calendar year, Japanese fiscal year (Apr-Mar), factory acceptance, repair, retrofit, and all-factory national output. Annual figures cannot be placed directly on dated events without classification.

primary_anchor.description: Sagami Army Arsenal production sheet explicitly labels Fiscal Year and months Apr..Mar, and contains separate production/repair/value classes.
primary_anchor.implication: At least one major postwar source series is fiscal-year accounting, not calendar-year output.

ChiHe.monthly_Japanese_series: 5 in Feb 1944 + 10 in Mar 1944 = 15 in FY1943
ChiHe.decision: Do not place 15 Chi-He in calendar 1943 without an independent dated factory source.

Type97.decision: Retain separate series; do not average.

KeNi.warning: The commonly repeated 1943 total may include repairs or fiscal-year effects in some source chains. New-build and repair must be separated.

mandatory_fields_for_each_future_number: factory coverage: one arsenal / named manufacturers / national
promotion_rule: No monthly or dated production ledger is promoted from an annual total alone. If only an annual/fiscal total exists, use a marked reconstruction band and preserve the source-basis uncertainty.

impact_on_previous_working.1935_1941_opening_ledger: Remains a useful scaffold but its 1941 monthly new-build curve is NOT authoritative. Opening 7-Dec physical/accepted Shinhoto estimate is retained as an engineering working band because it is tied to the separate 68-hull conversion order, not merely to the annual 507 figure.
impact_on_previous_working.1942_v001: Superseded for dated production by v002. The 525 new-Shinhoto point estimate was too confident before fiscal/calendar reconciliation.
